title: Design System: PhoneDock site
scope: Public landing page in site/ only. The Mac app design guide is design/DESIGN.md.

scrim.note: Fixed in both themes. Used as rgb(7 7 11 / alpha) in every scrim gradient and as the devices stage ground.

term-glass.note: Fixed. The agent card body, over a 16px backdrop blur.

phone-rim.note: Fixed. The 2px metal rim ring in the phone lift.

themes.mechanism: CSS light-dark() on :root with color-scheme light dark. data-theme="light" or "dark" on <html> forces a theme, stored in localStorage as pd-theme and applied before first paint.
themes.showBands: The hero, use cases and handoff sections carry .show, which forces color-scheme: dark in both themes. The nav is dark-scheme until scrolled past 24px.

display.purpose: Hero headline only, max 9.5em. Below 820px it is clamp(2.125rem, 9.4vw, 2.75rem). The closing heading uses 800 weight at 116% width, clamp(2.5rem, 5.2vw, 4.75rem), -0.035em.

lede.purpose: The opening statement of What it is, capped at 44ch.

quote.purpose: Prompts in the More prompts to try run-sheet.

run-prompt.purpose: The quoted prompt in each use-case run. The plain Instagram line is 480 in ink-2.

title.purpose: Setup step titles, device names, use-case app names, More prompts to try, Privacy and limits subheads (680 to 700, 1 to 1.25rem).

sub.purpose: Lines under section headings, in ink-2, max 38rem.

small.purpose: Captions, use-case answers and notes; the agent card prompt (560) and answer.

caption.purpose: The demo note under the agent card and the call count beside each answer.

tab.purpose: The three task tabs above the agent card.

label.purpose: Uppercase condensed column labels in the How it works diagram.

mono.purpose: Inline tool calls and commands; tabular clock digits in the agent card.

term-call.purpose: phonedock · name(args) lines in the agent card log.

code-block.purpose: Flow YAML and terminal output in the prompt book.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: The agent card, with backdrop-filter: blur(16px) saturate(1.2).

shadows.name: phone-lift
shadows.purpose: The CSS phone frame: rim rings and a long soft drop.

shadows.name: window-lift
shadows.purpose: The real app window on the devices stage. Below 820px: 0 0 0 1px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.12), 0 24px 48px -20px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.85).

shadows.name: hub-lift
shadows.purpose: PhoneDock card in the How it works diagram.

shadows.name: stage-edge
shadows.purpose: Hairline edge of the devices stage.

shadows.name: heading-glow
shadows.purpose: The handoff heading over its mood image.

shadows.name: icon-drop
shadows.purpose: App icon in the closing section, as a filter.

atmosphere.name: hero-scrim

atmosphere.purpose: Left scrim over the defocused desk photo, fading into the band below. Below 1200px: one top-to-bottom scrim.

atmosphere.name: hero-grain

atmosphere.purpose: Film grain so the defocused plate reads as film.

atmosphere.name: phone-pool
atmosphere.purpose: Cool light pool behind the hero phone. Booth light, not state colour.

atmosphere.name: handoff-mask
atmosphere.purpose: Masks the handoff mood image in from the left (30% below 1080px, none below 820px).

atmosphere.name: fleet-scrim
atmosphere.purpose: Darkens the blurred phones image behind the app window.

atmosphere.name: log-fade
atmosphere.purpose: Top fade on the agent card log once it is full.

shapes.phone: Proportional to --pw: bezel 3%, outer radius 15%, screen radius 12%, screen aspect 1072 / 2400, status strip 4.4% tall with a punch-hole camera (radial-gradient), plain black strip on the iPhone clip.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Every CSS transition and keyframe on the page.

motion.name: key-state
motion.purpose: Key border and background. Press is 0.12s with a 1px drop.

motion.name: lamp
motion.purpose: Lamp dot lighting on hover or focus.

motion.name: nav
motion.purpose: Nav wash, blur and rule after 24px of scroll.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Section blocks fade up once on entry, only when reduced motion is not requested.

motion.name: hero-settle
motion.purpose: The hero photo settles in on load.

motion.name: prompt-type
motion.purpose: The agent card types the real prompt.

motion.name: call-in
motion.value: 0.42s, translateY(8px) and opacity 0 to none, 0.07s stagger
motion.purpose: A call line lands at its time in the clip.

motion.name: answer-type
motion.purpose: The answer types, then the next run starts.

motion.name: step-light
motion.purpose: Handoff step lights follow the recording (3s, 7s, 13.5s).

motion.name: wire-packet
motion.purpose: Packets along the diagram wires while visible. Off with reduced motion.

motion.name: pool
motion.purpose: Closing light pool brightens from 0.25 to 1 opacity when in view.

breakpoints.name: hero-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Hero stacks: copy, then the demo centred; vertical scrim.

breakpoints.name: mid
breakpoints.purpose: Gutter 40px, section padding 96px. Nav links hide. Runs and devices two across.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Gutter 20px, section padding 72px. Demo one column with the phone first. Runs become a swipe carousel. Handoff mood image above the heading, steps stack. Prompt book pages stack.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Demo reorders to tabs, phone, card, note so it fits one view; prompt clamps to 2 lines, log 128px.

breakpoints.name: small
breakpoints.purpose: Keys share the row width, GitHub label hides, device kinds one column.

fallbacks.heroReducedMotion: The first run's poster frame and its whole transcript (prompt, calls, more line, answer) shown at once, held, with Play to start.
fallbacks.clipFailure: A clip that has not loaded 10s after its prompt leaves the run as static text.
fallbacks.freeze: ?at=<run>,<seconds> freezes a run at a moment for screenshots.
fallbacks.screenReaders: The typed card is aria-hidden; a visually hidden line gives the whole run (prompt and answer) at once.
fallbacks.recordings: Every clip shows its poster and waits for Play under reduced motion, and plays only while on screen.

imagery.real: Screen recordings (run-*.mp4, instagram, handoff) and a frame of the real app (app-window.webp), each with a provenance JSON beside it.
imagery.mood: AI-generated stills (bg-desk, mood-phones, mood-faceid): defocused, scrimmed or masked, credited in the footer, never presented as recordings.

narrative.northStar: The Stage Seen from the Booth
narrative.overview:
The page is a stage manager's view of a show that really happened. A plain black phone plays real screen recordings while, beside it, a dark terminal card titled Claude Code prints the agent's real calls as they land in the clip and ends on its real answer. Dark mode is show mode: matte black tinted indigo, cool light pools, film grain over a defocused night desk. Light mode is work-light mode: the app's pale stage grey with white paper and graphite ink. Both themes come from one set of `light-dark()` custom properties on `:root`, and three show bands (the hero, the use cases and the handoff) stay dark in both.

Saturated colour belongs to state. The three control colours from the Mac app (agent purple, you indigo, needs-you orange) mark who is in control, and the accent indigo fills the primary key. Everything else is ground, paper, ink, hairline rules and booth light. Sections are long ruled lists and column grids on the bare ground, with very few boxed containers. Real footage carries every claim: the hero reel, the four use-case runs, the handoff recording and a frame of the real PhoneDock window. AI-generated stills appear only as mood, defocused, scrimmed or masked, and are credited in the footer.

Motion is gentle and always optional. The typed prompt, the landing calls, the reveals, the wire packets and the recordings all have a still path under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and every recording carries a Pause/Play control. There are no libraries, no Three.js and no WebGL: static HTML, one stylesheet and two small modules.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes from one token set, switched by `light-dark()` and a stored toggle; show bands force the dark scheme.
Archivo variable, expanded and heavy for headlines. JetBrains Mono only for tool calls, commands and YAML.
Buttons are cue-light keys with a lamp dot.
State colour appears only as round ring-and-core lights, lamp dots, progress rails and state-coloured text or fills.
Hairline-ruled lists (run-sheet, setup steps, handoff steps, FAQ) carry most sections.
Real recordings in a plain CSS phone frame, synced to a terminal card of the agent's real calls.

rules.name: The State Colour Rule
rules.body: Purple, indigo and orange mean agent, you and needs-you everywhere on the page. Don't use them for decoration. Cool booth light (the indigo pool behind the hero phone, `booth`, `pool`) is lighting, not state, and stays low-alpha.

rules.name: The Shared Palette Rule
rules.body: Control colours match `design/DESIGN.md` exactly, per theme. New state colours start in the app's guide, then come here.

rules.name: The Show Band Rule
rules.body: The hero, the use cases and the handoff force `color-scheme: dark` in both themes, so the footage always sits on show black. The nav reads in the dark scheme over the hero and follows the page theme once scrolled.

rules.name: The Wide Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines use Archivo at 110% to 116% width with negative tracking (-0.028em to -0.035em). Body text stays at 100% width.

rules.name: The Typed Text Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only for tool calls (`get_ui`, `tap`, `request_human`), shell commands, the agent card's call lines and clock, and flow YAML or terminal output. Prose, prompts, answers, labels and buttons never use it.

rules.name: The Inner Padding Rule
rules.body: A bordered or filled container keeps at least 8px of inner padding between its edge and its content.

rules.name: The One View Rule
rules.body: On a phone the hero demo (tabs, phone, card, note) fits one viewport, so a call lands in view while the screen changes.

rules.name: The Lit Is Live Rule
rules.body: Light marks what is active: the running call wears the purple ring, the active task's rail fills purple, the lit handoff step follows the recording, the phone in play stands in a light pool, and the closing pool brightens when it scrolls into view.

dos: Do take every colour from the custom properties on `:root` and give each new token a light and dark value through `light-dark()`; only show-band darks are fixed.
Do keep agent purple, you indigo and needs-you orange tied to agent, person and help-needed states, matching `design/DESIGN.md`.
Do make buttons as keys: a lamp dot, 10px corners, 48px height, hairline border, and the indigo fill only for the primary action.
Do set headlines in Archivo at 110% to 116% width, 760 to 800 weight, with negative tracking.
Do keep JetBrains Mono for tool calls, commands, YAML and terminal output.
Do keep at least 8px of inner padding in any bordered or filled container.
Do give every moving element a reduced-motion path and every video a visible Pause/Play control.
Do let real footage carry every claim: screen recordings, the agent's own calls and answers, frames of the real app. Mark each shipping raster's origin in its sidecar JSON.

donts: Don't present an AI image as a recording or let it carry a claim about what the product did.
Don't name or show the real phone's brand or model; the phone frame stays a plain black slab.
Don't crop footage so a privacy blur becomes the subject.
Don't build fake product UI (drawn screens, mock phones, a 3D stage); show the real thing.
Don't use the state colours as decoration, gradients or section tints.
Don't set prose, labels or buttons in JetBrains Mono.
Don't add hard offset shadows. Lifted objects use the long, soft, negatively spread shadows listed above with a hairline or rim edge.
Don't use front-of-house theatre imagery (curtains, masks, velvet, marquee bulbs).
Don't put a small uppercase label above a section heading. Condensed caps are kept for diagram column labels and the Beta tag.
